title: Reward-component scale, variability and correlation analysis for the BWSN-1 PPO environment (MEASURE ONLY, not train)
status: MEASUREMENT COMPLETE. Reward formulations are PROPOSED, NOT approved. No weights chosen, no PPO training, observation (STEP 7) and action space (STEP 6) unchanged.

env.determinism: EPANET's hydraulic solver is deterministic. No stochastic input is used anywhere in Phase 5; leak-node selection and leak-coefficient allocation are closed-form functions of pipe length, so no random seed is required. Recorded seed: none used.

scope_statement: Validation/characterisation only. Every number is produced by the EPANET solver from the working copy with native controls and rules untouched, under the mandated solver policy and the Phase 5 leakage instrument. No optimisation, no search, no reward tuning, no RL.

service_node_policy.rule: declared elevation exactly 0.0 ft AND zero total base demand -> connector artefact, excluded from every service/safety statistic but KEPT in the hydraulic model

leak_instrument.status: VALIDATION INSTRUMENT, not a calibrated field leakage model (brief 18). Half-pipe-length weights, single closed-form global scale, exponent 0.5 from the file's [OPTIONS].

sizing.closed_form: k = target / sum_j (w_j * p_baseline_j^alpha); single evaluation, no optimisation of any kind.

actuator_effort_analytic.note: Static runs have zero step-to-step movement, so the REALISED movement/smoothness scale depends on the (not-yet-existing) policy action sequence and is a training-time HYPOTHESIS. The effort term MUST be computed on the COMMANDED normalised action (not realised pump speed, which the native STATUS rule can reset to 1.0 or 0 -> reward-hacking / closed-pump ambiguity).

proposed_normalization_constants.note: FIXED constants measured once (baseline reference run / this analysis) and frozen; NOT per-episode running statistics -> no train/eval leakage. deficit_ref guards against a ~0 baseline deficit by taking max(baseline mean, pooled p95).

leakage_only_collapses_service.description: A leakage-ONLY reward pushes pressure to the PRV lower bound; measure whether service degrades there.
leakage_only_collapses_service.verdict: service must be protected explicitly; a leakage-only reward is not safe by construction (see boundary check).

pressure_only_raises_leakage.verdict: maximising pressure inflates leakage; objectives oppose.

scale_imbalance.verdict: raw components span very different magnitudes; a raw weighted sum is dominated by the largest -> fixed normalisation is required before weighting.

sparse_or_degenerate_signal.verdict: negative-pressure count is (near-)always zero in bounds -> a pure hard-violation term is sparse; the smooth deficit / min-pressure terms carry the dense safety signal.

actuator_penalty_domination.verdict: unnormalised movement (L2^2 up to 28) would dominate normalised leakage/service terms (~O(1)); the effort term MUST be normalised by its analytic maximum.

reward_hacking_closed_pump_ambiguity.verdict: effort/smoothness MUST use the COMMANDED normalised action; realised pump speed is reset to 1.0 by STATUS-IS-OPEN or 0 when closed (G12), so penalising realised speed is gameable and mis-attributes native-rule behaviour.

boundary_seeking_safety.verdict: the leakage optimum sits at the PRV lower bound; this single corner is characterised here only. Exhaustive joint in-box safety is a STEP-9 (safety layer) + STEP-12 (tests) job; a safety term/clamp is required, not optional.

proposed_formulations.name: normalized_weighted_sum
proposed_formulations.formula: r_t = - w_L*(leak_t/leak_ref) - w_U*(unserved_t/req_ref) - w_P*(deficit_t/deficit_ref) - w_A*(||da_t||^2 / L2sq_max) [- w_E*(power_t/power_ref)]
proposed_formulations.note: dense, differentiable; every term normalised to ~O(1). Weights NOT tuned here.

proposed_formulations.name: constrained_penalty_service_protected
proposed_formulations.formula: r_t = -(leak_t/leak_ref) - LAMBDA*(deficit_t/deficit_ref) - BIG*max(0, n_below20_t) ; LAMBDA >> 1, BIG >> LAMBDA
proposed_formulations.note: minimise leakage subject to a large, explicit service/safety penalty; service is protected by construction.

proposed_formulations.name: baseline_relative_improvement
proposed_formulations.formula: r_t = (leak_ref - leak_t)/leak_ref - w_U*(unserved_t - unserved_ref)_+ / req_ref - safety_penalty
proposed_formulations.note: interpretable as fractional leakage reduction vs the NATIVE controller; naturally zero-centred at the baseline.

proposed_formulations.name: safety_first_lexicographic
proposed_formulations.formula: if any svc node < 20 psi (or < 0): dominant negative penalty; else minimise leak_t/leak_ref; effort as tie-break
proposed_formulations.note: encodes the priority hierarchy safety > service > leakage > effort; typically realised via masking / large penalties and pairs with the STEP-9 safety clamp.

constants.note: FIXED constants measured once (baseline reference run / this analysis) and frozen; NOT per-episode running statistics -> no train/eval leakage. deficit_ref guards against a ~0 baseline deficit by taking max(baseline mean, pooled p95).

limitations: Static-command runs: realised actuator MOVEMENT is 0, so the effort/smoothness scale is analytic (from bounds), not measured - HYPOTHESIS.
Leakage is a VALIDATION instrument, not field-calibrated; only RELATIVE leakage response is meaningful, never an absolute leakage claim.
Component scales measured on a representative in-bounds set (reference, corners, per-PRV edges); interior/mixed-corner joint safety is a STEP-9/STEP-12 job, NOT claimed here.
Pump power is HYDRAULIC (rho*g*Q*dH), no efficiency curve; an energy term is optional and clearly labelled.
next_step: Researcher review of the PROPOSED formulations and of the measured scales; then select ONE formulation + weights as a separate approved decision. STEP 9 safety layer must supply the hard clamp the boundary-seeking check shows is required.
